info.name: Doriath API Contract Suite
info.description:
Newman/Postman API-contract tests for the Doriath (vault) Nextcloud app. Locks the HTTP contract of doriath's controllers (appinfo/routes.php + lib/Controller/*): secrets, encryption suites, CA status, folders, secret-types, and the public link-share access endpoint. Every family is exercised for a happy path, an error/validation case (4xx, not 500 where the controller is correct), and an authorization case (no auth -> 401, or 404 for the public token route). The suite is self-contained and idempotent: it creates the vault objects it needs (a secret, a folder) and deletes them again in teardown.

This suite asserts the Phase-0 fixes: secret create returns 201 with ownerType:"user" (not 500); secret/suite/folder reads return their list/object shape; the public link-share token route is reachable without NC auth and 404s on an unknown token.

Most vault WRITES that mint or use key material (suite create, private-key upload, link-share create) require the in-browser RSA crypto flow and an unlocked vault with a freshly-generated key — they are not drivable from a headless API client and are QUARANTINED honestly below (covered by Playwright). What IS drivable from the API is the full secret CRUD round-trip, folder create, and all the reads + authz, which this suite exercises. That used to depend on the AMBIENT state of a long-lived dev vault that already had an unlocked suite; the CI job installs a FRESH Nextcloud where the caller has none, and every secret write was refused by SecretService::getActiveSuiteOrBlock(). Worse, the refusal is invisible from the status line — these are OCSController routes and Nextcloud's OCSMiddleware rewrites a 403 into an OCS v1 envelope served as HTTP 200 with the real code in ocs.meta.statuscode. The suite therefore PROVISIONS its own precondition: 'SETUP: ensure the caller has an active encryption suite' uploads a real, committed test RSA-4096 public key when (and only when) the caller has no active suite. The suite no longer assumes any ambient vault state.

AUTH MODEL: collection auth is noauth; every authenticated request carries an EXPLICIT basic-auth block (admin:admin via adminUser/adminPass). The no-auth requests target {{noAuthBase}} (127.0.0.1) so the host-scoped NC session cookie established on {{baseUrl}} (localhost) is never sent to them. Run with --ignore-redirects. See run-newman.sh.

GAP-4 FIX (previously quarantined): SecretController::create and EncryptionSuiteController::create now declare their required params nullable and validate presence in the body, so OMITTING a required field returns a clean JSON 400 instead of NC's reflection param-injection 500 HTML page. EncryptionSuiteController::create additionally catches InvalidArgumentException from the key-signing path, so an invalid public key also degrades to a 400. The corresponding create-error tests now assert 400 (not the old quarantined 500).

item.name: 0. AppHost observability (declarative health + metrics)
item.description:
Locks the ADR-006 / ADR-040 observability contract that src/manifest.json declares and OpenRegister's AppHost GenericHealthController / GenericMetricsController serve. These scenarios live in openspec/specs/apphost-adoption/spec.md and were previously waived with '@e2e exclude API-only endpoint — covered by the OR AppHost Newman contract collection'. That collection is in the OPENREGISTER repo and doriath's CI never runs it, so the contract was asserted NOWHERE for doriath. These requests assert it here, in doriath's own always-run collection.

Health is PUBLIC (auth-posture delta, ADR-006) so it is fetched from {{noAuthBase}} with no auth block — the host-scoped NC session cookie established on {{baseUrl}} is never sent there, keeping 'anonymous' honest.

item.name: 10. Metrics admin-only posture (non-admin -> 403)
item.description:
openspec/specs/apphost-adoption/spec.md — Requirement: Admin-Only Declarative Metrics Endpoint, Scenario: Non-admin user cannot scrape metrics. ADR-006 tightens the pre-adoption any-authenticated-user posture to admin-only.

WHY THIS FOLDER RUNS LAST, AND WHY IT MEASURES THE CALLER.

Newman keeps ONE cookie jar per HOST. Nextcloud resolves a request's session BEFORE it looks at an Authorization: Basic header, so a request that carries non-admin Basic credentials to a host where an ADMIN session cookie already exists executes AS THE ADMIN. An assertion of 'non-admin gets 403' written that way reads 200 and is then mis-filed either as a missing guard or, after someone 'fixes' it, as a passing test that never involved a non-admin at all.

Two defences, both required:
  1. The non-admin requests go to {{noAuthBase}} (127.0.0.1), where the admin session established on {{baseUrl}} (localhost) is not sent. This folder is placed LAST so the non-admin session it establishes on 127.0.0.1 cannot in turn pollute the anonymous no-auth assertions in folders 4 and 7, which run earlier against the same host.
  2. A CONTROL request immediately before the assertion calls /ocs/v2.php/cloud/user on the SAME host in the SAME chain and asserts the resolved identity is the non-admin user. If the control reports 'admin', the 403 assertion below is meaningless and the control fails first, naming the reason.
